notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, general vs a course stage (during-work vs general) for privacy and bias rules not tied to a stage; resolved to general. (2) actor, admin vs all or instructor for institutional statements, tool-access statements and advice to faculty; resolved by who the sentence binds or addresses. (3) policy_type: P56 vs P02 for the welcoming institutional posture (P02), P63 vs P35 for the advice to test assignments against AI (P35), P29 vs UNCOVERED for the rule to list team members on collaborative work (UNCOVERED, not about AI), P06 vs P01 for the mixed policy's default ban (P01), P44 vs P02 for the SEAS belief that AI can enhance learning (P02), P04 vs P05 for the choice among sample policies (P04, with the tiers coded as a separate P05 unit). (4) modality, informs vs may/should/must for sentences that describe a suggested use or consequence; resolved by whether the sentence tells the addressee what to do. (5) unit_stance: disclosure and misconduct sentences are neutral or permit, not require or restrict, because they are conditions or procedures; instructor-use suggestions on the teaching page are encourage. Units found by one coder: A over-coded narrative descriptions of faculty practice, event lists and a link title (dropped); B coded one rhetorical analogy (spell-checking) and a mission-statement clause (dropped). Kept single-coder units were distinct rules: clauses the other coder folded into a neighbouring unit (final responsibility, enforce integrity policies, students told of privacy risk, practice problems, clear communication condition), one principle, and resource pointers. Where each coder coded half of one sentence, units were merged. Stance: both coders delegates for the OUE and harvard.edu/ai pages; for the SEAS page A coded delegates and B coded encourage, resolved to encourage because the page states a welcoming position and delegates nothing.
